reason: The section separates Minister self-help, Crown disposal of property, and cost recovery.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister entry and actions to carry out an order to comply
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions authorize entry, force, possession, restoration, removal, disposal, and other measures.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify what the Minister may do to effect compliance with an order.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown ownership and disposal notice for property taken under an order
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections vest taken property in the Crown and require publication before some disposals.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize when property becomes Crown property and when disposal notice is required.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Recovery of order-compliance costs as Crown debt
proposedGroups.reason: The final provisions impose liability, joint liability, certificate filing, judgment effect, costs, and interest.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Trace how Crown costs become recoverable debt with interest.

reason: The target gives an overriding removal or disposal power for abandoned low-value property.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Disposal of low-value abandoned property on Crown Lands

focusSelections.evidenceText: value of the property or thing is $500 or less

proposedGroups.reason: The rule is tied to property abandoned, placed, or left on Crown Lands.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when low-value property on Crown Lands may be removed or disposed of.

reason: The section authorizes immediate action for safety, health, or environmental danger and cost recovery.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Immediate Crown Lands action for public safety, health, or environmental danger
proposedGroups.reason: Both subsections address emergency entry/action and recovery from the responsible person.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the emergency action and cost recovery power for dangers on Crown Lands.

reason: Posting authority, posted-land prohibitions, exceptions, and proof rules are distinct learning topics.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Posting Crown Lands to protect safety, health, or the environment
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection authorizes signs or notices controlling Crown Lands use for protective purposes.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Minister may post signs or notices controlling Crown Lands use.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibited conduct, exceptions, and offence for posted Crown Lands
proposedGroups.reason: These provisions prohibit contraventions and sign interference, list exceptions, and create a category C offence.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine who may enter despite posted restrictions and what conduct is an offence.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Proof of authorized posting and sign existence
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection creates presumptions for Department signs and signs existing before and after the conduct.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the proof rules for prosecutions based on posted Crown Lands signs.

reason: The target contains only a repealed section note and has no current operative study content.
The target states the Minister forest-protection power across Crown, Crown-vested, and private lands.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister power to protect forests from fire, insects, and disease

focusSelections.evidenceText: protect forests, whether on Crown Lands, other lands vested in the Crown or private lands

proposedGroups.reason: The rule covers fire, insect, and disease protection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the lands and hazards covered by the Minister forest-protection power.

reason: The section authorizes spray operations for forest-protection purposes, subject to named limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Aerial or ground spray operations for forest protection

focusSelections.evidenceText: carry out or cause to be carried out an aerial or ground spray operation

proposedGroups.reason: The power is tied to section 73 purposes and subject to section 75 and the Pesticides Control Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the authority and statutory limits for forest spray operations.

reason: The section provides the request process for excluding private lands from spray operations.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Private land owner request for exclusion from spray operation
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover the owner request, timing and content, and reasonable compliance steps.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the timing, content, and compliance rules for excluding private land from a spray operation.

reason: The section limits nuisance or trespass actions against the Crown to actual injury or property damage.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Crown nuisance or trespass liability for forest protection operations

focusSelections.evidenceText: actual injury to a person or actual damage to property

proposedGroups.reason: The rule applies to acts incidental to sections 73 and 74.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine when a nuisance or trespass action may lie for forest protection operations.

reason: The target grants the Minister power to build and maintain necessary forest roads.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister construction and maintenance of forest roads

focusSelections.evidenceText: construct and maintain any forest road he considers necessary

proposedGroups.reason: The power is for administration of the Act.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the Minister authority to construct and maintain forest roads.

reason: The target ties forest road construction and maintenance to prescribed standards.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Regulated standards for forest roads
proposedGroups.reason: The section is focused on the regulatory standard source.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the standard-setting source for forest roads.

reason: The section authorizes forest-road closures and requires signs and barricades.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Closing forest roads to travel
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover closure by vehicle or person class and posting after closure.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the Minister power and posting duty for closed forest roads.

reason: The offence section separates prohibited road conduct from penalty and proof rules.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibited conduct on forest or logging roads
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection lists prohibited travel, sign interference, unauthorized barricading or signs, and obstructive unattended vehicles.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify conduct prohibited on forest or logging roads without lawful authority.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Penalty and proof for forest-road signs and barricades
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections create a category C offence and presumptions for Department signs, notices, and barricades.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the penalty category and evidentiary presumptions for forest-road offences.

reason: Operational powers over logging roads are separate from rehabilitation and Crown non-liability.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Licensee powers to construct, restrict, and abandon logging roads
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection allows construction, travel restriction, and abandonment under plans or sales.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify logging-road powers of timber rights holders.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rehabilitation duty and Crown non-liability for logging roads
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require rehabilitation unless the Minister accepts responsibility and exclude Crown liability.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize the rehabilitation obligation and Crown liability limit.

reason: Granting reserved-road portions and the legal effects of registration are distinct.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minister grant of portions of reserved roads
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allow setting apart and granting only if other access serves the area.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when the Minister may grant part of a reserved road.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Mineral ownership and public passage after reserved-road grant
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections preserve Crown minerals and extinguish public passage on registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine mineral and public-passage effects of a reserved-road grant.

reason: The section authorizes reserved-road closures only with other access and requires posting.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Closing reserved roads to travel
proposedGroups.reason: The subsections cover closure authority, other-access condition, and signs or barricades.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Apply the conditions and notice duty for closing a reserved road.

reason: The reserved-road offence section separates conduct prohibitions from penalty and proof.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Prohibited conduct on closed reserved roads
proposedGroups.reason: This subsection lists travel, sign interference, unauthorized signs or barricades, and obstructive vehicles or equipment.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify conduct prohibited on reserved roads without lawful authority.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Penalty and proof for reserved-road closure signs
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections create a category C offence and a presumption that signs or barricades were posted by the Minister.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine the penalty category and proof presumption for reserved-road closure offences.

reason: The reserved-road discontinuance section has a definition, procedural steps, vesting rules, and public-passage effects.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Access definition and order to discontinue a reserved road
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections define access, authorize discontinuance with other access, and require registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the access concept and procedural steps for discontinuing a reserved road.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Freehold vesting after discontinuance based on boundary lines
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections allocate title based on boundary-line circumstances and defer vesting until registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Determine who receives title to a discontinued reserved-road portion and when.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Minerals and public passage after reserved-road discontinuance
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections preserve Crown minerals and extinguish public passage on registration.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recognize mineral ownership and public-passage consequences of discontinuance.
